questions: Was gpt-6-astra/high used only for a genuinely necessary phase-wide or cross-cutting architecture-lead role in the next P1 orchestration run?
How did its architecture hold up under independent specification review and downstream implementation?

applicability.description: The first Bundesliga P1 orchestration run after the workflow-improvement PRs.

questions: How much work and wall time did compaction recovery require?
What occupied context before and after recovery, and which reads were avoidable?

applicability.description: Orchestration sessions that compact or exercise recovery behavior.

questions: Did hot recovery and the compact-preview contract reduce recovery work without weakening safety?

applicability.description: The first orchestration run using the hot-recovery and compact-preview contract from ADR-0075.

questions: Is the heavy-operation memory policy too restrictive?
What outcomes, paging or OOM symptoms, and causal queue delays occurred in the 1.00–1.10 GiB experimental band?

applicability.description: Orchestration sessions that sample or exercise heavy-operation admission.

questions: How much waiting was caused by genuine owner or external gates versus avoidable agent-created blocking?

applicability.description: Orchestration sessions with owner decisions, external dependencies, or queued ready work.

questions: How often did correction limits trigger reconciliation, and what graph, contract, or implementation was reconciled?
Which model and reasoning-effort combinations were used for every reconciliation, was each role classified correctly, what did independent review find, and did the result remain stable downstream?

applicability.description: Orchestration sessions with review corrections or explicit graph/contract reconciliation.

questions: Where did review and correction churn occur, how many cycles were needed, and what acceptance bottlenecks caused it?

applicability.description: Orchestration sessions that use independent specification, implementation, or final review.

questions: How much useful parallelism was achieved and what writer-wave throttle was chosen?
Which ready work was blocked by the actual graph, ownership, review, integration, worktree, disk-reservation, or heavy-lease constraints?

applicability.description: Orchestration sessions that schedule multiple ready or potentially ready lanes.
